messages.subject: Node inconsistent with parents
parts:
G'day all,

Sorry for the multiple topics in a short time, but I've been running into an issue with all types of models I have thus far tried to fit in JAGS (CJS mark-recapture, N-mixture, and Multinomial mixture models). When I leave the NAs as NAs in my response data, I am often met with the "Node inconsistent with parents" error. 

Beginning parallel processing using 3 cores. Console output will be suppressed.
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  one node produced an error: Error in node y[2,3,3]
Node inconsistent with parents

Often, when I a priori impute some values for these missing occasions, the model runs fine. But sometimes, even when there's no NAs, I get the same error. When I test my model with short chains, I'll sometimes just try to run JAGS a few times until it doesn't provide this error and the model continues to run.

Does anyone know what's causing this error and how I can work around it? At the moment, when I do want include my missing occasions as NAs, I'll have to run the model quite a few times before I finally don't get this error message...

Kind regards,
Matt

messages.author: 373abc8c186a6d7e
messages.subject: Re: Node inconsistent with parents
parts:
Hi Matt,

This sounds like an issue with the initial values. Are you specifying them for that y variable? If not, doing so probably will fix the issue. I generally set them to match the exact value of y in the data or y+1 and one of those typically works.

I’m guessing the reason it occasionally works now is that the default random number generator occasionally picks compatible values for all of the initial values.

Hope this helps,

Frank

Hi all,

Thanks for your quick responses. Denis, I think you may be right that it has to do with initial values, but I'm really struggling to troubleshoot it. Perhaps you can see what's happening in the code? 

André, no NAs in the covariates, and I'm actually still having these issues when I've imputed the NAs in my response. Thus, I'm having these inconsistent parent node issues without a single NA anywhere in the data.

So, I'm trying to run a multi-season multinomial mixture model. Small mammals were trapped at 6 sites, for 4 consecutive nights, for 17 consecutive years. Every trapped mammal had its fur clipped to allow identification of recaps. I have my data organised in a c(6,4,17) array, where each value is the number of new animals caught. Thus, the data is a removal sampling type design which I've tried to analyse with the conditional multinomial model from section 7.6 in Kéry & Schaub (2015) AHM Vol. 1, extended to multiple years. 

## Model 1: Conditional multinomial

str(bdata<-list(y=y[,,-14],ncap=ncap[,-14],site=nrow(y),survey=ncol(y),year=dim(y[,,-14])[3],rain=rain6[-14],rainp=rainp[-14],fire=fire[,-14])) # 14th year is removed because there's no data

# Model

cat(file="Nmulti_conditional_fuscipes.txt"," # Model for Rattus fuscipes only
    model{
    
    ## Priors
  
    # Abundance model 
    
    alpha0 ~ dnorm(0,0.001) # Abundance intercept
    r ~ dunif(-1,1) # Annual population growth rate
    alpha1 ~ dunif(-5,5) # Effect of rainfall in past 6 mo
    alpha2 ~ dunif(-5,5) # Effect of fire history, which varies per year and site
    
    # Random site effect 
    
    for(i in 1:site){
      eps[i] ~ dnorm(0,tau.l) # Random site effect on abundance
    }
    tau.l <- pow(sigma.l,-2)
    sigma.l ~ dunif(0,5)
  
    # Detection model
    
    beta0 <- logit(p0) # Convert intercept to logit scale to assign uniform prior below
    p0 ~ dunif(0,1)
    beta1 ~ dunif(-5,5) # Effect of rainfall in week before survey on capture probability

    ## Conditional multinomial cell probabilities
    
    for(k in 1:year){
      for(i in 1:site){
        pi[i,1,k] <- p[i,k] 
        pi[i,2,k] <- p[i,k] * pow((1-p[i,k]),1)
        pi[i,3,k] <- p[i,k] * pow((1-p[i,k]),2)
        pi[i,4,k] <- p[i,k] * pow((1-p[i,k]),3)
        pi0[i,k] <- 1 - (pi[i,1,k] + pi[i,2,k] + pi[i,3,k] + pi[i,4,k])
        pcap[i,k] <- 1 - pi0[i,k]
        for(j in 1:survey){
          pic[i,j,k] <- pi[i,j,k] / pcap[i,k]
        }
        
        # Detection model 
        
        logit(p[i,k]) <- beta0 + beta1*rainp[k]
        
        # Model specification in three parts
        
        y[i,1:4,k] ~ dmulti(pic[i,1:4,k], n[i,k])
        n[i,k] ~ dbin(pcap[i,k], N[i,k])
        N[i,k] ~ dpois(lambda[i,k])
        
        # Log-linear model for abundance 
        
        log(lambda[i,k]) <- alpha0 + 
                            r*(k-1) + 
                            alpha1*rain[k] + 
                            alpha2*fire[i,k] + 
                            eps[i]
      }
      totalN[k] <- sum(N[,k]) # Pooled abundance per year
    }
    }
    ")

# Initial values

inits<-function(){list(N=ncap[,-14]+2, # ncap is total number of Rattus fuscipes caught over the 4 nights per site
                       alpha0=runif(1),r=runif(1),alpha1=runif(1),alpha2=runif(1),sigma.l=runif(1),
                       p0=runif(1),beta1=runif(1),sigma.p=runif(1))}

# Parameters

params<-c("totalN","alpha0","r","alpha1","alpha2","sigma.l","beta0","p0","beta1","sigma.p")

# MCMC

nc <- 3 ; ni <- 10 ; nb <- 2 ; nt <- 3 ; na <- 0 # Short chains to test model

# Output

Nmulti_conditional_fuscipes <- jags(bdata,inits,params,"Nmulti_conditional_fuscipes.txt",
                        n.chains = nc, n.iter = ni, n.burnin = nb, n.thin = nt, n.adapt = na,
                        parallel=TRUE)

Trying to run this model with short chains gives me the following error without fail:

Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : 
  3 nodes produced errors; first error: Error in node y[1,1:4,1]
Node inconsistent with parents

If anyone is keen to give it a shot with the data, let me know. Any help is greatly appreciated! The model does seem to run with the Poisson formulation of the multinomial mixture model (section 7.6.3), but I've lost a bit of faith because the conditional multinomial was working fine until yesterday as well!

Looking forward to your answers. :)

Regards,
Matt
